Hello Team,

it was a good meeting today regarding the additional street trees on the bank. Thank you all for joining and your honest feedbacks.

Background:

*
There are a series of street trees already planted on the project as per approved permits. Photo attached.
*
Due to space and terrain limitations no more than 36” rootball trees could have been planted which is what is seen in the photo. And they were spaced apart 30’ or more due to City recommendations
*
Clients didn’t like their small canopy size which was dictated by the rootball size and wanted to double teh density.
*
One option was to add another tree in between along the same line as approved trees which would ahve been more difficult to get approvals on as they are on City land outside PL.
*
It was then discussed in one site meeting with the Client to add a staggered row of trees on the bank within our property as indicated in the current Street tree layout plan.

Being on the bank with steep slopes and already installed TECCO mesh, there are other complexities highlighted for which we had this meeting today with Dave (DRS) and Josh (Geo-Tech)

*
Dave and Josh confirmed that what is proposed is achievable from technical standpoint but permitting may be very difficult if not impossible.
*
If this is feasible, we would like to explore this through Guillermo (CREST) for any permitting requirements.
*
The penetrations in the TECCO mesh will be kept at a minimum to accommodate similar size trees that are already planted, - 3’ dia and ~ 30’ apart.

Dave will look into details for these penetrations and can provide any technical drawings needed to support permit efforts and eventually construction.
*
Structural and Josh will need to work together with HCC for the 3’ tall semi-circular retention methods to avoid erosions at these penetrations points where trees will be planted.
*
Landscape will be looking at plug planting for this slope through the Tecco mesh for quicker plant establishment and ground coverage to avoid surface run-offs.

@Steve & @Cezar - Can you please provide your thoughts on the retention methods which may also help David and Guillermo in their review of things.

it is understood that this may be a very challenging task but not ruled out as impossible so lets work together and give our best efforts.
Thank you all.
